system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

content.text:
# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: AWS
G2: GCP
G3: software development
G4: Go beyond terratest

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Filling the 2020-2022 or 2024 gaps with invented jobs or stretching neighbouring date ranges
T2: Disclosing more private/medical detail than needed (father's death) instead of a neutral 'career break' if anything
T3: Claiming AWS or GCP for multi-cloud ads
T4: Calling him a software developer or claiming Python/Go development
T5: Old cover letter targets an IT Administrator job and says 'available to start immediately' - no longer true
T6: The CV lists skills first; writer should keep dates accurate when reordering

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

maintaining Terraform infrastructure as code, and automating service deployments. Part of a

applications. Earlier experience includes Windows/Linux administration and leading a 60-server
migration to Azure without unplanned downtime.

Networking and security: TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, hub-spoke network design, VNet

Systems: Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Windows Server, VMware, Active Directory, Microsoft 365

Cloud Engineer (contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.
Mar 2025 - Present

infrastructure-as-code maintenance.
• Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps

frequency increased from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
• Operate AKS upgrades, node pools and ingress; developers own application manifests.
Professional Development and Contract Search
Feb 2024 - Feb 2025
• Studied Terraform and earned the Terraform Associate certification in 2025; built a Proxmox
homelab.
• Completed a three-month, part-time online cloud bootcamp taught in English in Dec 2024.
Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed
Sep 2022 - Jan 2024
• Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5-40 employees.
• Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing
and backups.
• Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint / OneDrive.
Career Break | Family Care
Mar 2020 - Aug 2022
• Provided full-time family care, maintained Azure administration knowledge and offered unpaid IT
help to church and family.
Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Jan 2014 - Feb 2020
• Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
• Planned and led the migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate,
Azure VMs, VNets and site-to-site VPN; completed cutovers over six weekends without unplanned
downtime.
• Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
• Provided second-line escalation support for network and Active Directory issues.
Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Aug 2011 - Dec 2013
CERTIFICATIONS
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003), 2025
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), 2019
EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College, 2011
LANGUAGES
Dutch (native), English (fluent), Twi (spoken)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707
Corvale Mobility
Application: Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor - Fleet Connectivity
Dear Hiring Manager,
Corvale Mobility’s fleet connectivity project calls for infrastructure that is secure,
maintainable and ready for production. I bring hands-on Azure infrastructure engineering,
Terraform networking and automated deployment experience relevant to that challenge. In my
current contract at Havenstad Logistics, I am part of a three-person team operating
approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions.
My work on Azure landing zone networking includes Terraform modules for hub-spoke VNets,
Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints and cross-subscription peering. I added
Terratest module tests in the pipeline and nightly drift detection to support ongoing
maintenance. This provides a practical foundation for contributing to your
infrastructure-as-code repository and network design. My cloud experience is Azure-based,
matching your acceptance of other major clouds alongside AWS.
I also replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure
DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS. For
most applications, deployment frequency increased from roughly monthly to several times per
week. I operate AKS upgrades, node pools and ingress, while developers retain ownership of
application manifests. Earlier, I planned and led a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration,
completing cutovers over six weekends without unplanned downtime. These projects
demonstrate both delivery leadership and attention to reliable operations.
Your team’s remit combines early architecture decisions with responsibility for production
infrastructure. I would bring experience connecting network design, infrastructure automation
and service deployment, supported by a background administering Windows and Linux
systems and implementing practical security controls. I would welcome a discussion about how
this experience could support the platform linking Corvale’s new trains to its backend services.
Kind regards,
Samuel Achterberg-Osei

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
